title: Gunmen Fire at Tiger Shroff's Car in Juhu; Actor Unhurt, Two Injured
excerpt: Three motorcycle-borne assailants shot at the actor's car near Pushpa Park on Sunday evening. Mumbai Police formed 15 teams, and an unverified social media post in the Lawrence Bishnoi group's name claimed responsibility.
body:
• Three motorcycle-borne gunmen fired at actor Tiger Shroff's car in Mumbai's Juhu area at about 7 p.m. on Sunday, October 18; Shroff was not injured.
  • His driver, Firdosh, was shot in the left hand and taken to Nanavati Hospital, and a bystander, Yogesh Chavan, 28, was also shot and admitted to Cooper Hospital.
  • Mumbai Police have formed 15 teams and are scanning CCTV footage; a social media post in the name of the Lawrence Bishnoi group claimed responsibility, but police have not verified it.
  • For readers in Mumbai: the claim circulating online is unconfirmed, the motive is still unclear, and police are asking Shroff about any recent threat calls as the manhunt continues.

Three unidentified men on a motorcycle opened fire on a car carrying Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff in Mumbai's Juhu neighbourhood on Sunday evening, injuring his driver and a bystander but leaving the actor unharmed, police said. The shooting took place at about 7 p.m. near Pushpa Park, also known as Jamnabai Nursery, roughly 350 metres from Juhu police station, according to The Times of India.

What Happened in Juhu

Police said Shroff had attended a celebration at Pushpa Park and was preparing to leave when the three assailants, dressed in white shirts, fired at his car and fled towards SV Road and Vile Parle railway station. The Times of India reported seven rounds were fired at the vehicle. Driver Firdosh suffered a bullet injury to his left hand and was taken to Nanavati Hospital. Yogesh Chavan, 28, who was standing nearby, also sustained a bullet injury and was admitted to Cooper Hospital.

https://x.com/AdityaRajKaul/status/2111860820070256705

Police initially said Shroff had suffered slight abrasions from glass fragments after the car's windows shattered. Deputy Commissioner of Police (West Zone 2) Mohit Garg later clarified that the actor was not injured. Shroff's father, actor Jackie Shroff, also confirmed to reporters that his son was safe.

The Bishnoi Claim and the Police Response

Within hours, a social media post attributed to Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu claimed responsibility for the attack in the name of the Lawrence Bishnoi group. The post alleged that Shroff had been warned by phone and was targeted over his association and work with Salman Khan, and it threatened others in Mumbai's film industry who work with Khan. Police said they were verifying the post and had not authenticated the claim.

"We had called and warned him, but he did not understand. Therefore, today we made him understand in a stronger way."

— Social media post attributed to Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu, as reported by IANS

Juhu police and Mumbai Crime Branch officers formed 15 special teams to trace the assailants, examining CCTV footage from the area to identify them and establish their escape route, IANS reported. Police were registering a first information report and seeking details from Shroff about any recent threat calls or warnings. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis called the Mumbai Police Commissioner to ask about the incident and directed a swift investigation and strict action against those responsible.

A Pattern of Attacks Linked to the Khan Feud

The unverified claim fits a pattern investigators have described before. On April 14, 2024, two men on a motorcycle fired shots outside Salman Khan's Galaxy Apartments residence in Bandra; investigators alleged that attack was ordered by jailed gangster Lawrence Bishnoi and his brother Anmol Bishnoi over grievances linked to the 1998 blackbuck hunting case, in which Khan was accused of killing an animal revered by the Bishnoi community. Former Maharashtra minister Baba Siddique, a politician close to Khan, was shot dead in Bandra East on October 12, 2024, and Crime Branch charge sheets have linked that assassination primarily to the Bishnoi network. Police have not said the Juhu firing is connected to those cases, and the social media claim remains unverified.

The shooting drew sharp political reaction. Congress leader Sachin Sawant called it "utterly shocking" and pointed to the Siddique murder and the firing at Khan's home, while Mumbai Congress president Varsha Gaikwad asked whose responsibility it was to ensure the safety of Mumbaikars if such incidents keep happening.

What Happens Next

The immediate focus is the manhunt. Fifteen police teams are working through CCTV footage along the escape route towards Vile Parle, and investigators are checking whether Shroff received threat calls before Sunday, which would help establish whether the attack was planned around the Bishnoi claim or had another motive. The condition of the two injured men, and whether police authenticate the social media post, are the next facts to watch.
